segments.narration: Thousands of ping pong balls vanished inside a Minnesota waterfall. At Devil’s Kettle, half the river drops into a hole and disappears.
Locals dropped dye, logs, and tracking gear down the throat. Nothing ever floated out into Lake Superior.
Was the Earth drinking an entire river into deep subterranean caverns? The mystery stumped geologists for decades.
In 2017, hydrologists measured the river’s water flow. The volume above and below the falls was identical.
Immense water pressure inside the kettle crushes logs and balls into tiny pieces instantly. But if the exit is right there, how did every heavy object stay trapped inside?
